# Erdős–Rado Sunflower Conjecture

Collaboration beta

Must every sufficiently large family of distinct sets of one size contain three distinct sets with identical pairwise intersections?

$$\exists C<\infty \phantom{\rule{.28em}{0ex}}\forall r\ge \mathrm{1,}\phantom{\rule{1em}{0ex}}{f}_{3}\left(r\right)\le {C}^{r}$$

Erdős Problem #20

Known results and sources ↓

Image: Three translucent uniform-set forms meet in one dark common core while their gold and emerald petals remain disjoint, introducing the three-petal sunflower question without claiming a proof.Three petals share one core: the geometric pattern whose unavoidable appearance is still conjectural at exponential scale.On this pageProblem

Research problem

## Exact mathematical statement

Let $f_3(r)$ be the largest cardinality of an $r$-uniform family of distinct finite sets containing no three distinct members $A,B,C$ with

$$A\cap B=A\cap C=B\cap C.$$

Their common intersection is allowed to be empty. The three-petal sunflower conjecture asks whether

$$\exists C<\infty\;\forall r\ge1,\qquad f_3(r)\le C^r.$$

The same absolute constant must work independently of the rank and ground-set size. Only the three-petal case is in scope; no reduction to every fixed number of petals is claimed.

The current approach studies finite transversal codes over arbitrary finite coordinate alphabets. Three codewords form a sunflower exactly when all three equality labels agree. The conjecture remains open: the source reports local reductions and scoped checks, but no global contradiction.

Statement boundary Research question, not proof evidence

The route map and retained computations do not by themselves establish this statement.

## Problem at a glance

Three r-element sets form a three-petal sunflower when their three pairwise intersections are the same core R, equivalently when their petals outside R are pairwise disjoint. The right vignette is a binary transversal-code baseline: {0,1}ʳ has 2ʳ codewords and is sunflower-free in the code model; interpreting each word x as its transversal r-set Aₓ gives the corresponding r-uniform construction. The conjecture asks whether every sunflower-free r-uniform family nevertheless has size at most Cʳ for one absolute finite C. The general case remains open.

# Comparisons of Three-Phase Systems for Generating a High-Frequency Rotating Magnetic Field Powered by Rectangular Signals

14 Pages Posted: 24 Apr 2023

See all articles by Andrzej Skumiel

## Andrzej Skumiel

Adam Mickiewicz University

### Abstract

The article compares two versions of 3-phase systems for generating a rotating high-frequency magnetic field f = 100 kHz powered by rectangular signals with appropriately shifted phases. Obtaining sinusoidal signals from square waveforms was obtained using passive filters consisting of capacitors and inductors. The magnetic system was housed in a ferrite torus. In one version the filter branches were connected in a delta-system (Δ) and in the other version they were connected in a (Y)-system. The delta-system delivered a 72% higher magnetic field strength than the (Y)-system at the same supply voltage. Similarly, it turned out that the delta-system gives more than 3.5 times the temperature increase rate dT/dt compared to the (Y)-system. The advantage of the delta-system is its high efficiency, which can be used in magnetic hyperthermia as a treatment supporting radio- or chemo-therapy.

Keywords: Apparatus for generating a rotating magnetic field, High frequency electromagnetic system, Rotating magnetic field, Magnetic fluids, Magnetic hyperthermia.

### Abstract

This study discusses metal(loid) accumulation in the Kızılırmak Delta system (Samsun, Türkiye) using a multilayered approach. 15 metal(loid), including As, Cd, Hg, Pb, Cr and Ni, were studied in 5 different lagoons, the Kızılırmak River, and the Black Sea as a whole. Environmental pollution, bioaccumulation, and human health risks were evaluated in an integrated manner. While contrasting hydrological seasons were chosen for water and sediment samples, we focused our biotic sampling on the wet season to capture the period of peak metal(loid) accumulation. Data were analyzed using sediment assessment indices such as the enrichment factor (EF) and the contamination factor (CF) (Layer 1), bioaccumulation indices such as BAF, BSAF, and MPI (Layer 2), along with non-carcinogenic (THQ, HI) and carcinogenic risk indices (CR, TCR) that are important for public health (Layer 3). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
